subject: Transportation Systems
title: Dredging and Depth
description: A quick win: understand Dredging and Depth.

hook.text: The biggest container ships need 52 feet of water beneath them. Most harbors aren't naturally that deep.

buildup.text: Dredging ships scoop sediment from the bottom, deepening channels so large vessels can enter safely.

discovery.text: Silt builds up constantly. Ports must dredge year-round just to maintain existing depths.

twist.text: Dredging is expensive and environmentally controversial—disturbing seafloor habitats and releasing toxins.

climax.text: Ports that can't dredge deep enough lose business to competitors. Depth determines which ships can call.

punchline.text: The depth of the harbor decides the wealth of the city.

quiz.question: Why do ports need constant dredging?
options: Silt accumulates and shallows the channel
